summary: All 51 LRE requirements implemented across 15 Java files; build clean. Six judgement calls flagged for human review.

issues.title: HCM entry velocity: 0 m/s (LRE-FR3) vs 0.1 m/s (system description)
issues.raw: LRE-FR3 says 'On entering HCM, the LRE advises a velocity of 0 m/s'. system_description.txt says HCM is 'Reduced speed (0.1 m/s)'.
issues.fix_directive: Implemented LRE-FR3 (0.0 m/s) because the structured requirement is the canonical input. If 0.1 m/s is intended, amend LRE-FR3.

issues.title: CAM has no specified entry output
issues.raw: LRE-FR4 says CAM 'performs evasive manoeuvres' but names no advised velocity or heading; LRE-DM7 restricts outputs to advVel/advHdng.
issues.fix_directive: No output is emitted on entering CAM. If an evasive advisory is required, LRE-FR4 must state its value.

issues.title: Safe large distance for absent obstacles
issues.raw: LRE-DM5 requires odist/hdist/vdist to 'return a safe large distance' when no obstacle exists, without giving a value.
issues.fix_directive: Sensor.SAFE_LARGE_DIST = 1000.0 m. Any value well above the 1 m thresholds preserves the intended guard polarity.

issues.title: Relative-speed floor in CalcCPA
issues.raw: LRE-OP5 does not define cda/tcpa when the relative speed is zero, which is the 'no dynamic obstacle and stationary AUV' case its own Sensor defaults produce.
issues.fix_directive: MIN_REL_SPEED_SQ = 1.0E-9 is added to the squared relative speed so tcpa stays finite instead of NaN.

issues.title: cstc/cdyn annotated nat but carry -1
issues.raw: LRE-Var5/LRE-Var6 call cstc and cdyn natural numbers and also give -1 as the 'no obstacle' value; the ETL maps Java int to RoboChart nat unconditionally.
issues.fix_directive: Followed the requirement literally; the controller never tests for -1, the Sensor absorbs the absent-obstacle case via safe defaults, so no guard depends on the unrepresentable value.

issues.title: Literal 1 vs named threshold in LRE-Beh4
issues.raw: LRE-Beh4 says odist to cdyn and cstc must be 'greater than 1' without naming a threshold, while neighbouring requirements name thresholds explicitly.
issues.fix_directive: Used the literal 1.0 where the requirement gives a bare number and LreConstants only where a threshold is named. If LRE-Beh4 means minSafeDist, say so.
